newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Brief outburst of firing in Sierra Leone capital.
newsitem.headline: Brief outburst of firing in Sierra Leone capital.

text.p: Heavy mortar fire and shooting rang out briefly across Sierra Leone's capital Freetown, causing panic in the city where many fear a Nigerian attack to restore ousted president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, witnesses said.

A spokesman for the May 25 coupmakers said the outburst, which lasted 10 minutes late on Tuesday, followed a quarrel between Sierra Leonian and Nigerian soldiers at the island airport of Lungi off the capital.
There was no independent confirmation of this version of events.
Regional giant Nigeria, acting in the name of Sierra Leone's West African neighbours, has reinforced its troop presence in Freetown to reinstate Kabbah who was deposed by junior officers.
Nigeria previously had troops there under a West African defence pact.

On June 2, Nigerian gunboats shelled the city and its forces clashed with dissident Sierra Leone soldiers and their rebel allies, who took up arms in 1991 and have flooded into the capital since the coup.

Since then, a tense calm has prevailed, with the coup leaders saying that they would consider fresh elections but would not have Kabbah back. They accuse him of stalling on peace with the rebels and humiliating the army and fomenting ethnic hatred by arming Kamajor traditional hunter militias.

Kabbah, who is in neighbouring Guinea, won 1996 elections which ended four years of military rule in Sierra Leone, one of the world's poorest nations, despite mineral riches such as diamonds. The latest military coup was the third in five years.
